studies.Study: Deckers IA et al. (2014) [PMID: 24327014] — estimate 1 · Mixed sex; models adjusted for sex
studies.Reference: Long-term dietary sodium, potassium and fluid intake; exploring potential novel risk factors for renal cell cancer in the Netherlands Cohort Study on diet and cancer.
studies.Title: Long-term dietary sodium, potassium and fluid intake; exploring potential novel risk factors for renal cell cancer in the Netherlands Cohort Study on diet and cancer.
studies.Authors: Deckers IA, van den Brandt PA, van Engeland M, Soetekouw PM, Baldewijns MM, Goldbohm RA, Schouten LJ
studies.Design: Prospective cohort study with case-cohort design
studies.Population: Netherlands Cohort Study participants aged 55–69 years with histologically confirmed epithelial renal cell carcinoma
studies.Gender: Mixed sex; models adjusted for sex
studies.Smoking Status: Non-current/current smoking status, with duration and intensity included in adjustment
studies.comparison_type: Per increment of 1 g/day of potassium intake

sample_size.excerpt: The Netherlands Cohort Study (NLCS) with case-cohort design included 120,852 participants aged 55-69 years.

cases.excerpt: After 17.3 years of follow-up, 485 RCC cases and 4438 subcohort members were available for analyses.

effect_size.excerpt: Participants with high sodium and low fluid intake compared to those with low sodium and low fluid intake had a higher RCC risk (HR(95% CI): 1.91(1.10–3.32)). Other interactions between sodium or discretionary salt intake and RCC risk factors were not significant (data not shown).
effect_size.location: Table 2, Renal cell cancer risk according to indicators of sodium intake, fluid intake and potassium intake

confidence_interval.location: Table 2, fully adjusted potassium intake row
